key_insight: The Self-Supervised Semantic Bridge (SSB) learns to align semantic representations between source and target domains so unpaired image-to-image translation can retain high visual fidelity and better generalize—without depending on target-domain adversarial losses or perfect diffusion inversion.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between adversarial and diffusion-inversion approaches: it avoids the generalization limits of target-domain adversarial training while overcoming the low-fidelity outputs caused by imperfect inversion into diffusion latents.
method: Learn a self-supervised semantic bridge that aligns high-level features across source and target domains, creating a shared semantic space for translation.

Use the bridge to guide a diffusion-based generation pipeline (or hybrid adversarial-diffusion setup), reducing reliance on exact noise-latent inversion and on target adversarial loss during training.
Train with domain-agnostic, self-supervised objectives (feature consistency, semantic reconstruction) to preserve content and improve out-of-distribution generalization.
impact: SSB enables practitioners to produce more faithful and generalizable unpaired translations, improving workflows in image editing, domain adaptation, and data augmentation while reducing sensitivity to target-domain supervision or imperfect inversion.

paper_title: Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation via a Self-Supervised Semantic Bridge
paper_authors: Jiaming Liu, Felix Petersen, Yunhe Gao, Yabin Zhang, Hyojin Kim
